hook.situation: You're lost at Seoul Station. You need the bathroom urgently, but the signs are all in Korean. You try 화장실 어디예요? — and a local points down the hall, speaks three fast sentences, and walks away. You caught the direction but not the words. What do you say next?
objectives: Ask where something is using 이/가 어디예요? and 이/가 있어요?
Use 부터/까지 to describe time ranges (9시부터 6시까지) and routes (여기부터 역까지)
Deploy repair phrases — 다시 말해 주세요, 천천히 말해 주세요, 잘 모르겠어요 — to keep conversations alive
hook.whyItMatters: Travel Korean lives or dies on two skills: finding things and recovering when you get lost in a conversation. 부터/까지 turns you from someone who can only ask about single moments ('몇 시에?') into someone who can talk about ranges ('여기서 거기까지 얼마나 걸려요?'). And the repair phrases are the difference between a Korean who keeps talking to you and one who switches to mime.

grammarNotes.title: N부터 / N까지 — from … to … (ranges in time and space)
grammarNotes.func: 부터 marks where a range starts and 까지 marks where it ends — "from A to B." They work for time (아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지, from 9 to 6) and for place (집부터 학교까지, from home to school), and each can appear alone too (부터 = "starting from," 까지 = "up until / by").

formTable.when: Start point of a range (attaches to any noun)
formTable.ex: 아침 → 아침부터 · 한 시 → 한 시부터

formTable.when: End point of a range (attaches to any noun)
formTable.ex: 저녁 → 저녁까지 · 여섯 시 → 여섯 시까지
내일 → 내일까지 · 다섯 시 → 다섯 시까지

examples.en: I work from nine to six.
examples.note: Classic time range: 부터 on the start time, 까지 on the end time.

examples.en: It's far from home to school.
examples.note: Place range with 부터…까지. You'll also often hear 집에서 학교까지 — see the key point below.

examples.en: From what time is the movie?
examples.note: 부터 used alone to ask just the starting time.

examples.en: I'll read the book by tomorrow.

keyPoint.label: 부터 vs 에서 (both can mean "from")
keyPoint.body: For a starting point you measure a stretch from — especially time — use 부터: 아침부터 (from morning). For a physical place you set out from, native speakers usually say 에서: 집에서 학교까지 (from home to school). So time ranges lean on 부터…까지, while place ranges usually use 에서…까지. You'll still hear 집부터 학교까지, so it's not wrong — just know that 에서…까지 is the more common "place-to-place" frame. The full location particle 에서 gets its own chapter; for now just remember: time → 부터, place → often 에서, and 까지 marks the end either way.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 까지 starts with the tense consonant ㄲ, so keep it crisp — [kka-ji], not a soft [ga-ji]. After a 받침 like ㅂ/ㄱ/ㄷ, 부터 tenses a little: 집부터 sounds like [집뿌터].

drill.instruction: Make a "from … to …" sentence with 부터 and 까지, following the model.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 아홉 시까지 여섯 시부터 일해요. / 집까지 학교부터 멀어요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지 일해요. / 집부터 학교까지 멀어요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English says "from … to …," and learners often reach for 까지 first or swap the two particles. Tie each particle to its meaning, not to word order: 부터 always sits on the START point and 까지 always sits on the END point.

grammarNotes.title: V아/어 주세요 — asking someone to do something for you
grammarNotes.func: V아/어 주세요 is the polite way to ask someone to do something for you: "please (do) … (for me)." Take the verb stem, add 아/어 by vowel harmony, then attach 주세요. It powers the survival phrases you need in class and out on the street — 다시 말해 주세요 (please say it again), 천천히 말해 주세요 (please speak slowly).

formTable.when: Stem's last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ (bright)
formTable.ex: 받다 → 받아 주세요 · 보다 → 봐 주세요

formTable.when: Stem's last vowel is anything else (not ㅏ/ㅗ)
formTable.ex: 읽다 → 읽어 주세요 · 만들다 → 만들어 주세요
말하다 → 말해 주세요 · 일하다 → 일해 주세요
다시 → 다시 말해 주세요 · 천천히 → 천천히 써 주세요

examples.note: 말하다 is a 하다 verb → 말해. With 다시 ("again") it's the #1 classroom phrase.
천천히 ("slowly") + 말해 주세요 — use it when someone talks too fast for you.
With a plain noun, use 주세요 directly (no 아/어). 좀 softens it to "please / if you would."
읽다's last vowel isn't ㅏ/ㅗ → 읽어 주세요. The 주세요 adds the "for me" nuance.

keyPoint.label: V아/어 주세요 vs N 주세요
keyPoint.body: Plain 주세요 (from 주다, "to give") means "please give me ___" and attaches straight to a noun: 물 주세요, 책 주세요. But when you want someone to DO something for you, a bare noun won't carry it — you put the verb in the 아/어 form first: 책을 읽어 주세요 (please read the book for me). So: a thing you want handed over → N 주세요; an action you want done → V아/어 주세요. The deeper 주다 "do-it-for-me" grammar comes later; for now treat V아/어 주세요 as one fixed request phrase.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In 말해 주세요 the ㄹ links into 해 — [마래 주세요]. In 읽어 주세요 the hidden ㄱ of 읽 carries onto 어 — [일거 주세요]. Keep 주세요 light and even, don't stress it.

drill.instruction: Turn each verb into a polite request with V아/어 주세요, following the model.

englishSpeakerPitfall.wrong: 다시 말하 주세요 / 천천히 말하세요 (meaning "please say it again for me")
englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 다시 말해 주세요 / 천천히 말해 주세요
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Two traps. First, you have to conjugate to the 아/어 form before 주세요 — it's 말해 주세요, never the bare stem 말하 주세요. Second, plain 말하세요 is a polite command ("speak") with no "for me" warmth; adding 주세요 turns the order into a real request — exactly what you want when asking a teacher or a stranger for help.

exampleSentence.note: 이 follows consonant-ending 실 — subject particle, not topic particle

exampleSentence.en: How long does it take to the subway station?
exampleSentence.note: 까지 = as far as / to — the end-point of a distance range
몇 번 = which number — essential for subway navigation
A practical travel question when you need staff help, directions, or opening hours

exampleSentence.en: Where is the Line 2 boarding area?
exampleSentence.note: 타는 곳 = the place where you board; more natural than saying the line itself is an exit

exampleSentence.en: I'll study hard starting from today.
exampleSentence.note: 부터 attaches to the start-point — 오늘부터 means 'from today onward'

extendedVocabulary.english: to / until / as far as (end point)

exampleSentence.en: Until what time are you open?
exampleSentence.note: 까지 after a time = 'until' — perfect for asking business hours
다시 placed before the verb — it modifies the action (말하다)
천천히 before 말해 주세요 specifies the speed — add it any time you need less pace
잘 모르겠어요 is softer and more natural than just 몰라요 — 겠 adds an element of 'I think / I guess'

exampleSentence.en: I walk from here to the station.
exampleSentence.note: 걷다 is ㄷ-irregular: 걷 + 어 → 걸어요 (ㄷ changes to ㄹ before a vowel)
얼마나 걸려요? (How long does it take?) is a must-know travel question — 걸리다 expresses time cost
돕다 + 아/어 주다 → 도와주다 (ㅂ-irregular): 도와주세요 is a one-word survival phrase

exampleSentence.en: I'm looking for the subway station.
exampleSentence.note: 찾고 있어요 = currently searching (ongoing action) — useful when you're lost and need help

exampleSentence.en: It's a 10-minute walk from here to the station.
exampleSentence.note: 여기부터 = starting from here — pairs naturally with 까지 for distance ranges

extendedVocabulary.english: over there (that place in the distance)

exampleSentence.note: 저기 = yonder/over there (visible but farther away). 여기 = here, 거기 = there, 저기 = over there
으로 = direction marker (go via/toward). 왼쪽으로 가다 = go left

exampleSentence.en: There's a convenience store on the right.
exampleSentence.note: 에 있다 = something exists in that location — combine direction + 에 있다 to describe where things are
알겠어요 is warmer and more engaged than just 네 — it shows you actually processed what was said

extendedDialogue.setting: Jimin is a foreign learner at Seoul Station. She approaches 민준 (a station employee) looking confused.

lines.speaker: 지민
lines.en: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
lines.grammarNote: 저기요 = 'excuse me' to get someone's attention. 화장실이 — 이 attaches after the consonant-final 실.

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.en: It's to the right of that exit over there.
lines.grammarNote: 오른쪽에 있어요 — 있어요 + 에 for a static location, with 출구 as the landmark

lines.speaker: 지민
lines.ko: 죄송하지만 천천히 다시 말해 주세요. 잘 모르겠어요.
lines.romanization: Joesonghajiman cheoncheonhi dasi malhae juseyo. Jal moreugesseoyo.
lines.en: Sorry, but please say that again slowly. I don't follow.
lines.grammarNote: 천천히 다시 말해 주세요 — the V아/어 주세요 request, and the single most useful sentence in this chapter

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.ko: 네! 저기 출구요. 출구에서 오른쪽으로 가세요.
lines.romanization: Ne! Jeogi chulguyo. Chulgueseo oreunjjogeuro gaseyo.
lines.en: Yes! That exit there. From the exit, go to the right.
lines.grammarNote: 출구에서 marks where the movement starts; 오른쪽으로 marks the direction it goes

lines.speaker: 지민
lines.en: Got it! Thank you. And where is Line 2?
lines.grammarNote: 알겠어요 signals you understood — say it so the other person knows they can stop repeating

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.ko: 2호선은 왼쪽에 있어요. 여기에서 오 분 걸려요.
lines.romanization: I-hoseoneun oenjjoge isseoyo. Yeogieseo o bun geollyeoyo.
lines.en: Line 2 is on the left. It takes five minutes from here.
lines.grammarNote: 걸리다 is the verb for time taken; 여기에서 marks the starting point of that five minutes

lines.speaker: 지민
lines.en: From when until when is the information desk open?
lines.grammarNote: 언제부터 언제까지 — the RULER pattern with question words at both ends

lines.speaker: 민준
lines.ko: 아침부터 오후까지 열어요. 안내소에서 직원이 도와줘요.
lines.romanization: Achimbuteo ohukkaji yeoreoyo. Annaesoeseo jigwoni dowajwoyo.
lines.en: It's open from morning until the afternoon. The staff there will help you.
lines.grammarNote: 아침부터 오후까지 — the same ruler, both endpoints filled in; 안내소에서 marks where the helping happens

readingText.title: 지하철역에서 온 문자 (Text messages from the subway station)
readingText.body:
지민: 민준 씨, 지금 지하철역에 있어요. 그런데 여기를 잘 모르겠어요.
민준: 어디에 가요?
지민: 2호선을 찾고 있어요. 출구도 모르겠어요.
민준: 2호선은 왼쪽에 있어요. 여기에서 왼쪽으로 가세요. 오 분 걸려요.
지민: 알겠어요. 화장실도 찾고 있어요.
민준: 화장실은 출구 오른쪽에 있어요.
지민: 감사합니다! 그런데 안내소는 언제부터 언제까지 열어요?
민준: 안내소는 아침부터 오후까지 열어요. 지금 가도 돼요.
지민: 천천히 다시 말해 주세요. 아침부터 오후까지요?
민준: 네, 아침부터 오후까지요. 안내소에서 직원이 도와줘요.
readingText.bodyTranslation:
Jimin: Minjun, I'm at the subway station now. But I don't really know my way around here.
Minjun: Where are you going?
Jimin: I'm looking for Line 2. I don't know the exit either.
Minjun: Line 2 is on the left. Go left from where you are. It takes five minutes.
Jimin: Got it. I'm looking for the bathroom too.
Minjun: The bathroom is to the right of the exit.
Jimin: Thank you! By the way, from when until when is the information desk open?
Minjun: The information desk is open from morning until the afternoon. You can go now.
Jimin: Please say that again slowly. From morning until afternoon?
Minjun: Yes, from morning until afternoon. The staff at the information desk will help you.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Which way should Jimin go for Line 2, and how long does it take?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 왼쪽으로 가세요 (go left) — 오 분 걸려요 (it takes five minutes).

comprehensionQuestions.question: Where is the bathroom?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 출구 오른쪽에 있어요 — to the right of the exit.

comprehensionQuestions.question: Find every use of 부터 and 까지 in the text. Why is each one used, and why does one sentence use both?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 언제부터 언제까지 열어요? — Jimin asks for both ends of the ruler at once: 부터 for the start, 까지 for the end. 아침부터 오후까지 열어요 — Minjun answers with both ends filled in. 아침부터 오후까지요? repeats the whole range back to confirm it, which is exactly what 부터…까지 is for: one span, two endpoints.

culturalNote.title: 역 문화 — Subway Station Culture in Korea
culturalNote.body: Seoul's subway is one of the world's most navigated systems, and Korean stations are built around the assumption that you might not know where you are. Every exit is numbered (1번 출구, 2번 출구…), and Koreans give directions by exit number — not left or right from the entrance. So when someone says '2호선은 5번 출구예요,' they expect you to find exit 5 on the station map and orient from there. Station staff (역무원) are trained to help and are very patient with foreigners — they will often walk you part of the way. Don't be shy about using 다시 말해 주세요 or 천천히 말해 주세요. Korean station staff hear these phrases from tourists every day, and asking for a repeat is far more respected than nodding and wandering off confused.

inlineExercises.explanation: 부터 marks the start-point (9시부터 = from 9) and 까지 marks the end-point (6시까지 = to/until 6). 에 alone (9시에 / 6시에) would give two single time-points but not express a range. 에서 is for places where actions happen, not time expressions.
The V아/어 주세요 pattern uses 주세요 (from 주다 = to give, as a favor). 말해요 alone is a statement ('you say it again'). 주어요 is not a polite request form — 주세요 is the standard polite imperative of 주다.

inlineExercises.prompt: 다음 문장에서 틀린 것을 찾아보세요: '여기부터 역에서 걸어요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 에서 marks where an action happens (a stage), not a destination endpoint. The ending point of a range takes 까지 — '역까지' means 'all the way to the station.' 역에서 걷다 would mean 'walking at the station' (action happening there), not 'walking as far as the station.'

inlineExercises.prompt: A local just gave you fast directions. You didn't catch everything. What do you say?
inlineExercises.explanation: 천천히 말해 주세요 (Please speak slowly) is the best repair phrase when the issue is speed. 잘 모르겠어요 (I don't really know) signals confusion but doesn't ask for help. 다시 한 번 주세요 is missing the verb — it would mean 'give me one more time' (like asking for a second serving). 네, 알겠어요 would falsely signal comprehension.

inlineExercises.prompt: Translate: 'From Monday to Friday there is class.'
inlineExercises.hint: Which particle marks the start of a range? Which marks the end? What pattern says 'there is'?
inlineExercises.explanation: 부터 and 까지 mark the start and end of a range. 수업이 있어요 states that class exists or is scheduled during that range.

inlineExercises.prompt: 죄송한데, 천천히 말해 ___ . (Sorry, please speak slowly.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 말해 주세요 = the complete V아/어 주세요 request form. 말해요 alone = a statement or direct command, which would sound rude to a stranger. 주다 is the infinitive/dictionary form — you cannot end a polite sentence with a bare infinitive.

inlineExercises.prompt: 안내소는 오전 9시___ 오후 6시___ 열어요. Which pair of particles fits?
inlineExercises.explanation: This is a time range (opening hours), so you need the RULER pair: 부터 for the start (9시부터) and 까지 for the end (6시까지). 에 alone marks single moments, not ranges. 에서 is for physical locations where actions happen, not time expressions. Mixing 에서 or 에 with 까지 would be grammatically wrong here.
부터 marks the starting point of a time range. 까지 already marks the endpoint, so the natural pair is 9시부터 6시까지.
말하다 becomes 말해 주세요 in a polite request. 천천히 tells the other person to speak slowly.
다시 means again, and 말해 주세요 is the polite request. Together they form the repair phrase you use when you missed what someone said.

bullets: 부터/까지 = the RULER: draw a line between a start (부터) and end (까지) for time ranges and routes — 9시부터 6시까지, 여기부터 역까지
V아/어 주세요 = the FAVOR TICKET: swap any verb in front of 주세요 for any polite request — 말해 주세요, 써 주세요, 찍어 주세요
Repair toolkit: 다시 말해 주세요 (again), 천천히 말해 주세요 (slowly), 잘 모르겠어요 (I'm not sure) — use these freely and Koreans will respect you for it

writingTask.prompt: Write a 3-sentence text to a friend: tell them your office hours, then ask them to speak slowly and say it again.
writingTask.hint: Use N부터 N까지 for the time range, and V아/어 주세요 for the two requests (천천히 말해 주세요, 다시 말해 주세요).
writingTask.model: 저는 아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지 일해요. 천천히 말해 주세요. 다시 말해 주세요.
writingTask.modelEn: I work from nine to six. Please speak slowly. Please say it again.

canDo: Give a time or place range with N부터 N까지 (아홉 시부터 여섯 시까지)
Ask someone to do something for me with V아/어 주세요 (말해 주세요)
Ask for repetition or a slower pace when lost (다시 · 천천히)
Ask where a place is using survival words (화장실 · 출구 · 지하철역)
